business_scope.primary_industry_name: Non-Vessel Operating Common Carrier (NVOCC) Ocean Box Brokerage

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law heritage with customary law elements; statutory law for International Companies)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER) Plus
Samoa's WTO Membership Protocols, including GATS disciplines

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering and Prevention of Terrorism Act 2007 (Samoa), as amended; International Companies Act 1987, as amended; Financial Intelligence Unit registration and record-keeping obligations under the Money Laundering and Prevention of Terrorism Act; Registrar of International Companies supervision of licensed registered agents; MCIL/Registrar directives on beneficial ownership and source-of-funds documentation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of the ultimate beneficial owner's valid passport and any name-change evidence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the document-issuing jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or consular legalization by the Samoan competent authority where the issuing country is not an Apostille Convention party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address for each ultimate beneficial owner and proposed director (utility bill or bank statement dated within 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or bank, certified by a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or consular legalization where applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the shareholder/board consent to incorporation, including approval of memorandum and articles, appointment of the licensed registered agent, and registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public and licensed registered agent in Samoa or the signatory's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or consular legalization for signatures executed outside Samoa

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference and source-of-wealth/source-of-funds confirmation issued by the UBO's principal bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The maintaining financial institution, authenticated through notarization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or consular legalization depending on the bank's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified English translation and, if applicable, certified bilingual English/Chinese version of the International Company Memorandum and Articles of Association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator approved by the Samoan Registrar or duly qualified legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required for internal charter; charter copy certified by the licensed registered agent before filing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all ultimate beneficial owners, directors, and proposed signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, Samoa's domestic AML/CFT alert list, EU/UK consolidated sanctions lists, and an international politically exposed persons database. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, high-risk jurisdiction, source-of-wealth discrepancy, or third-party payment model in the NVOCC freight forwarder context. The licensed registered agent must document source of funds for any capital contribution and retain records for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Companies and International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) — International Companies Unit; name clearance is submitted through licensed registered agents or the MCIL e-service filing module.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory registered name must be in English or in a script approved by the Registrar; for Chinese-language use, the Chinese name is registered as a dual/trade name, must not be misleading, and must be accompanied by a certified romanized transliteration. The certificate of incorporation may issue in English with a Chinese-character trade-name endorsement. A Chinese-only charter and internal governance documentation are permitted as the governing internal contract, provided the registered agent maintains a certified English version for official filing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name rejection must be communicated by the Registrar with the stated ground. The applicant's licensed registered agent may file a written request for administrative review with the Registrar within 14 business days of rejection, attaching the name clearance application, the rejection notice, and any required ministerial approval or explanatory submission. If the Registrar upholds the rejection, an appeal may be filed with the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour under the International Companies Act, and thereafter by way of judicial review to the Supreme Court of Samoa. A name reservation that expires may be renewed only by a fresh application; extension requests should be lodged in writing before expiry and are generally granted for a further 30-day period upon payment of the applicable statutory fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional. A virtual office is acceptable only for the statutory registered-office address if it consists of a physical Samoan street address maintained by a licensed registered agent and staffed during business hours. A purely virtual address without a licensed Samoan registered agent is not permitted. For the NVOCC/freight forwarding licence, authorities may require evidence of substantive trade presence and local contactability before issuing the associated customs, port, or business licence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to medium. For a passive International Company with no physical operations in Samoa, the first-year unannounced physical inspection likelihood is estimated at 10%; where the NVOCC statutory licence or a Samoan Customs/trade licence is held, inspection likelihood increases to an estimated 20%. The licensed registered agent remains subject to periodic unannounced AML/CFT inspections by the FIU and Registrar.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987, as amended, Parts II and III; International Companies (Amendment) Act 2018; Companies Act 2001 (application to international companies only where expressly incorporated).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an International Company together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association, followed by issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; capital may be expressed in any currency and shares may be issued with or without par value. No escrow deposit requirement is imposed under the International Companies Act for ordinary international companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers to the Memorandum and Articles of Association of the International Company (Company No. WS-IC-2024-XXXX) hereby subscribe to and accept the allotment of one ordinary share each, fully paid, as recorded in the register of members. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at the office of the registered agent in Apia, Samoa, and that the registered agent be engaged to maintain the office in accordance with the International Companies Act 1987. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Name] and [Name] be appointed as Director and Secretary, respectively, each to serve until resignation or removal, with authority to open bank accounts, execute documents, and adopt a common seal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry, MCIL, via licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed international company name to the Registrar for clearance and reservation. The name must include a restricted suffix such as 'International Company', 'Limited', or 'IC'. File the name reservation request electronically or in person through the registered agent; obtain the Certificate of Name Reservation within the stated period.
required_dossiers: Copy of registered agent engagement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused for similarity or prohibited language, submit up to three alternative names for priority re-examination at no additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Memorandum and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent and notary public in Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage the licensed registered agent to draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, including the objects clause, authorized share capital, number of directors, and registered office clause. Have each subscriber and the initial director sign the document before a notary public; request the agent to execute its consent to act as registered agent.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (draft and final)
Consent to act as director and secretary
Subscribers' proof of identity and address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the governing law references or objects clause, supply a revised clause and re-notarize only the changed page, then re-submit within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Fee Remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry, MCIL, Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form IC-1 (application for incorporation) together with the executed Memorandum and Articles, registered agent consent, and prescribed government fee. Deposit the filing fee via bank transfer to the MCIL collection account or through the registered agent's trust account; retain the official receipt.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or queried, the Registrar issues a notification of defect; correct the stated defect (e.g. amending the capital narrative or adding a required signature) and resubmit within 15 business days to avoid lapse of the name reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry, MCIL, Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, dated from the time of incorporation, and registers the company in the International Companies Register. The registered agent shall collect two certified copies and the company extract.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate is not issued due to administrative delay, file a formal written request for expedited issuance; if the Certificate contains clerical errors, return it to the Registrar for reissuance under section 11 of the International Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Adoption of Corporate Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the International Company in Samoa or by written resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting to adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution, allot shares, adopt the registered office, appoint officers, and approve the opening of bank accounts and the issue of share certificates. Record the minutes, maintain the register of members, directors, and secretaries, and affix the company's common seal if adopted.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a procedural irregularity is discovered (e.g. quorum defect), ratify the action by subsequent written resolution signed by all directors or by convening a new valid board meeting within 7 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Filings and Tax Exempt Credential
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry and Samoa Ministry of Revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the company's registered details in the International Companies Register, pay the annual government levy (if payable), and obtain a certificate of tax status confirming the company is not resident for Samoa income tax purposes and is outside the scope of local stamp duty on offshore activities. Maintain the registered agent and disclose the agent's details to the Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax status certificate is delayed, rely on the Certificate of Incorporation and file a written reminder; if annual levy is under-assessed, provide corrected confirmation from the registered agent and obtain an amended receipt.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Maritime Division, Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI), Samoa Ports Authority for marine-related premises, and the Samoa International Companies Registry for offshore trade scope compliance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Non-Vessel Operating Common Carrier (NVOCC) Operating License under the Shipping Act 1975 (as amended) and the Samoa Freight Forwarding Licensing Guidelines

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) of Samoa, under the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 - Low Impact / Registration Level (Preliminary Environmental Assessment) because the principal activity is administrative office-based ocean freight brokerage and non-vessel operation; a Full EIA Report is only required if a warehouse or container-handling yard is developed in a sensitive coastal zone.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater discharge permitted; any sanitary effluent must be connected to a licensed public sewerage system or septic treatment system compliant with Samoa EPA water quality criteria. Stormwater runoff from parking areas must pass an oil-water separator. Air emissions shall be limited to negligible diesel generator backup uses; noise levels must not exceed daytime 55 dB(A) at the property boundary. Solid waste, including used packaging and abandoned cargo, must be stored in covered containers and removed to licensed landfills only.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority under the Fire and Emergency Services Act 2007, including emergency exit inspection and fire extinguisher maintenance. Structural load inspection for any office or warehousing facility must comply with the Samoa National Building Code. Occupational safety clearance must be obtained from the Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) Samoa, covering first aid provision, hazardous substance storage, and employee safety training for freight handling operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR) of the Independent State of Samoa, operating under the Tax Administration Act 2019; taxpayer e-services portal 'Molimauina' at https://molimauina.gov.ws; customs clearance administered by the Samoa Customs Service via the Asycuda World single-window system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned International Company (IC) obtains a Samoan Tax Identification Number (TIN) by filing Form TIN-01 Application for Registration with the Ministry for Revenue. The IC must be incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 and maintain a licensed registered agent and registered office in Samoa. Submission requires: certified copy of the certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, register of directors and shareholders, notarised passports of beneficial owners, an IC registered agent certificate, and a board resolution authorising TIN registration and appointment of a local tax representative where relevant. Non-resident applicants are registered immediately; documents in multilingual form are accepted in English or certified translation. There is no statutory minimum capital requirement. TIN issuance precedes VAGST registration and customs exporter code activation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no US-style check-the-box election. Under the International Companies Act 1987, an IC may by special resolution elect to convert to a local domestic company (triggering full Samoan income taxability and loss of offshore exemption), redomicile to another jurisdiction, or migrate into Samoa. For indirect tax, an IC may elect to register for VAGST on a voluntary basis below the WST 100,000 threshold or seek group registration for related entities. No hybrid mismatch elections arise for ICs because the offshore regime grants exemption from income tax and there is no controlled-foreign-company or hybrid instrument offset mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2009 (as amended by the VAGST (Rates) Amendment Act 2022)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 annual taxable turnover (mandatory); voluntary registration is permitted for persons making taxable supplies below the threshold; foreign entities supplying services to Samoa may be required to register if imports of services exceed the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory e-invoicing regime is in force. VAGST-registered entities must issue compliant tax invoices (VAGST Act s.30) showing supplier name and TIN, recipient name, description of supply, VAGST amount and rate. Monthly VAGST returns and payments are filed electronically via the Molimauina portal, with no statutory digital stamping or API-based fiscal clearance. Customs export declarations must be lodged electronically through the Asycuda World single-window platform. New rules require retained source records in electronic format to satisfy MfR audit queries.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: VAGST is zero-rated on (i) export of goods removed from Samoa (Schedule 1, VAGST Act 2009); (ii) international transport of goods, including ocean freight and NVOCC services rendered as principal or agent in connection with goods carried from Samoa; (iii) services physically performed outside Samoa and supplied to a non-resident; (iv) services ancillary to the export or international transit of goods, including inland haulage, port handling, containerisation and freight forwarding, provided the supplier obtains and retains documentary evidence that the service was performed for an export consignment. The supply must be invoiced to a non-resident recipient and paid for through a licensed Samoan bank to evidence foreign currency consideration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/Export Entry) filed via Asycuda World and processed by Samoa Customs Service
Bill of Lading (original, telex release, or express release) evidencing the NVOCC as contract carrier for the export consignment
Commercial export invoice and freight invoice issued by the NVOCC showing zero-rated VAGST treatment
Packing list and cargo manifest for the ocean shipment
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice from a licensed Samoan commercial bank proving receipt of the export freight proceeds in convertible foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to post-clearance audit by the Ministry for Revenue and Samoa Customs. Substantiation failure or fraudulent claims trigger: (i) a shortfall penalty of 50% of the tax understated, increased to 100% for intentional evasion, plus a 25% late payment surcharge (Tax Administration Act 2019, ss.73-78); (ii) criminal prosecution with fines up to WST 100,000 and imprisonment up to seven years (VAGST Act s.74); (iii) retrospective clawback of the unsubstantiated VAGST refund with monthly interest at 2%; (iv) cancellation of VAGST registration and denial of tax clearance certificates; and (v) exchange-control offences under the Exchange Control Regulations 1976 enforced by the Central Bank of Samoa, including daily penalties for non-repatriation of export proceeds within 180 days and revocation of the IC's offshore banking licence in egregious cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), acting as the Exchange Control Authority under the Exchange Control Act 1975 and the Exchange Control Regulations, together with the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Act 2019 (as amended).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoa tala (WST) is convertible for current-account transactions through licensed authorized dealers with standard documentary support and CBS reporting. Capital-account transactions require prior CBS approval or registration. A Samoa International Company (WS_IC) is treated as non-resident for exchange-control purposes; therefore, its external foreign-currency receipts, including ocean freight and NVOCC service revenues earned wholly outside Samoa, may be held offshore without mandatory conversion. Profit remittance and dividend distribution to non-resident shareholders are structurally permitted from external accounts and do not create onshore WST conversion pressure. The principal hurdles are the need for a CBS-licensed bank to be the settlement agent, strict economic substance documentation for dividend outflows, and the prohibition of using foreign currency for domestic Samoan transactions without dealer conversion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For resident Samoan entities, export proceeds from goods and services must be repatriated through an authorized dealer within 30 days of receipt, and 100% of repatriated proceeds must be offered for conversion into WST unless a specific 'external account' exemption is obtained from CBS. For the WS_IC NVOCC/Freight-Forwarding International Company, being non-resident, freight income originated from international ocean carriage and brokerage is external income and is not subject to the resident surrender requirement. However, any WST-denominated collections generated from Samoan domestic cargo or onshore logistics invoices will be classified as resident-source transportation revenue and will trigger the 30-day surrender rule with a mandatory conversion ratio of 100% unless the International Company applies for and receives a CBS non-resident account designation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low as a primary treasury settlement rail; Medium as an ancillary disbursement channel only. Offshore digital EMI providers such as Wise, Airwallex, Currenxie and similar platforms are not licensed or regulated by the Central Bank of Samoa and cannot directly access the Samoa clearing system, the local WST real-time settlement, or CBS reporting. Their use is legally constrained to white-label correspondent arrangements where the underlying value transfer is ultimately booked through a CBS-licensed commercial bank. Operating the NVOCC treasury solely through an unlicensed EMI creates a high AML/CFT non-compliance risk and may trigger unauthorized money-transmission exposure under Samoan law.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Initial corporate account opening for a Samoa International Company generally requires at least one director, or an authorized local registered agent with certified power of attorney, to attend an in-person KYC interview at the bank. CBS-licensed banks are increasingly requiring physical presence of the controlling shareholder or senior director for medium-risk enhanced due-diligence files, including the ISIC 5229/NVOCC freight-forwarding sector. Remote opening is occasionally considered where the bank can rely on a regulated offshore bank's KYC and a notarized board resolution, but it is not consistently available for International Companies and is subject to the bank's internal policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry red flag: NVOCC freight forwarders frequently execute payments to third-party ocean carriers, foreign agents and port operators without transparent ownership or cargo documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide licensed NVOCC / freight-forwarding certificate, annual business license, signed ocean carrier service contracts, house bills of lading and master bills of lading, commercial invoices, freight booking confirmations, and a documented flow-of-funds narrative matching each disbursement to an underlying consignment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk geographic concentration: cargo routes or counterparties touching sanctions-exposed territories trigger elevated CBS and correspondent-bank screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide transactional IP geolocation logs, cargo AIS tracking reports, container status data, counterparty corporate formation evidence, sanctions screening policy, negative news check reports, and a written internal policy for automatic prohibition of prohibited-jurisdiction cargo.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: International Company tax-haven profile combined with offshore ownership raises suspicion of concealed beneficial ownership or unverified source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the Samoa International Company registered agent certificate, register of directors and shareholders, written confirmation that no bearer shares are issued, CBS tax-exempt status letter, audited balance sheet or notarized shareholder wealth statement, and legal-entity structural chart evidencing the entire ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, rapid in-and-out clearing through the operational account is suspicious of round-tripping or criminally derived freight receivables.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide monthly reconciliation reports, sub-ledger of freight receivables and payables, an internal treasury policy explaining large same-day transfers, board approval minutes for treasury thresholds, and an agreement to implement a separate trust/escrow account for float management.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholder capital contributions must be sent by SWIFT MT103 to the WS_IC's USD or WST settlement account at a CBS-licensed commercial bank. The remittance must be annotated with the purpose code corresponding to 'foreign direct investment' or 'intercompany loan', the precise legal name of the International Company as beneficiary, and the underlying evidence, including the board resolution, share subscription document or loan agreement. The receiving bank will perform balance-of-payments (BOP) reporting to CBS. For capital injections in WST, or where the bank receives foreign currency and converts to WST, a Samoa authorized-dealer transaction report is required; however, external USD capital injection into a USD-denominated offshore account held within the bank may be retained in USD without conversion.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payment of ocean carriers, foreign haulage agents, port terminal operators and overseas logistics technology providers, the primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers and commercial letters of credit (sight or usance) issued through ANZ Bank Samoa or BSP Samoa. Correspondent-dollar clearing is commonly executed via U.S. correspondent banks. Payments to Philippine, Chinese, Fijian and New Zealand counterparties should use the MT103 with clear freight-invoice references and cargo identifiers. For onshore WST payments, the account must be debited in WST and settled locally; for foreign-currency payments, disbursement is made directly from the USD or other foreign-currency current account, avoiding unnecessary dual conversion. Trade finance facilities may be extended under documentary collection arrangements for vessel space or equipment-fleet bookings.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot foreign-exchange contracts for immediate conversion of USD freight receipts into WST or settlement currencies through a CBS-licensed authorized dealer.
Outright forward foreign-exchange contracts for up to 12 months, permitted by the authorized dealer when the underlying exposure is a bona fide current-account trade flow from NVOCC operations.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the WST arranged with an offshore counterparty, subject to the underlying trade documentation and the condition that no CET is made available in Samoa; the WST is treated as a non-deliverable currency in the offshore NDF market.

Cross-currency swaps between USD and EUR or USD and AUD where the freight-forwarding treasury maintains matched receivables and payables in those currencies and all swap legs settle outside the Samoan domestic payments system.
Tom-next and short-dated FX swaps with a licensed dealer for temporary liquidity bridge between freight collection accounts and payment accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of International Company (Form ICA-7)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the anniversary date of incorporation; extension up to 30 days available upon prior written application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 50 per month or part thereof; persistent non-filing for six months triggers administrative strike-off and dissolution under International Companies Act 1987, plus disqualification of directors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Exempt Company License Fee (Offshore Business Licence Renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) / Samoa International Finance Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January of each calendar year or within 30 days of the anniversary of issue for newly licensed entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Imposition of a 10% surcharge for payments after the due date; repeated default leads to licence suspension and prohibition of banking operations in Samoa

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: NVOCC / Ocean Freight Forwarding Statutory License Annual Declaration (if foreign-owned and operating a U.S. or third-country NVOCC office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Maritime Commission (FMC) for U.S. based NVOCC license; for Samoa-licensed entity, filing with MCIL/SIFA under the International Companies Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For FMC-licensed NVOCC, annual OTI annual tariff publication and financial responsibility renewal on the anniversary date of the FMC license
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: FMC may suspend or revoke NVOCC license, issue civil penalties up to USD 10,000 per day for unlicensed operations, and impose cargo hold orders

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit for a Samoa International Company solely by virtue of the International Companies Act 1987. However, audit becomes mandatory if (i) the company is a licensee under public-interest regulated activities, (ii) consolidated group turnover exceeds USD 1 million, or (iii) at least 10% of members holding at least 25% of share capital request an audit in writing
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by Samoa, or if declared in the annual return, Local GAAP (Samoa International Financial Reporting Standards equivalents) for exempt companies; always acceptable to prepare internal financial statements for audit exemption determination

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must file an annual confirmation of beneficial ownership with the Registrar, listing any changes in ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) that occurred during the reporting year. Share transfers and changes in UBO must be notified within 14 days of the event. The confirmation must be signed by a director or registered agent and must identify all individuals with 10% or greater interest or other controlling influence.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 1,200 per annum for licensed registered agent services in Samoa (including registered office, filing of annual return, and statutory mail forwarding)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 8,000 per annum for a typical exempt international company preparing English-language IFRS financial statements; no audit required for dormant or exempt companies unless triggered by thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for International Company offshore income; 27% for ordinary resident companies carrying on taxable activity in Samoa
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies are wholly exempt from Samoan income tax on income derived from international business outside Samoa. There is no capital gains tax, no branch profits tax, and no withholding tax on dividends paid by an International Company to non-resident shareholders. The exemption applies provided no business is carried on with Samoa residents and no Samoan-source income is derived.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR6 Company Income Tax Return filed through the Samoa Inland Revenue and Customs Authority (SIRCA) e-filing portal. A tax-exempt International Company is not required to file IR6 unless it derives Samoan-source income, but it must maintain annual accounts and file annual confirmation documents with the International Companies Registry.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than six months after the company's fiscal year-end. For a 31 December accounting period, the return and supporting financial statements are due by 30 June of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Insert the Samoan TIN issued by SIRCA for the International Company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Samoan IC TIN. Do not use a foreign TIN of the ultimate beneficial owner or home office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Business Activity and Industry Code
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Describe the principal activity and enter the relevant statistical classification code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For NVOCC and ocean freight forwarding operations, describe the activity as offshore freight brokerage and cargo consolidation; state that no local carriage is provided within Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross income subject to Samoan income tax. International Companies report only Samoan-source income; offshore freight forwarding income is exempt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero for non-resident-owned IC income arising from international ocean freight forwarding, NVOCC box brokerage, and related ancillary services performed outside Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim all allowable deductions directly related to taxable Samoan-source income. For exempt ICs, deductions are not required to be allocated.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule showing that all operating costs relate to offshore customers and non-Samoan vessel operations; claim no deductions against exempt income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Taxable Income and Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute taxable income after exemptions and apply the 27% corporate rate where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero tax payable for a qualifying International Company. If local-source sales or Samoan agency activities exist, self-assess tax at 27% and seek immediate professional advice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration by the director or registered agent that the information is true and correct.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident director may sign electronically; the agent must maintain a certified copy of the signed declaration in Samoa.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of a taxable IR6 return attracts a penalty of 20% of the tax assessed, plus a monthly late-payment surcharge of 2%, capped at 40% of the total tax due. An exempt International Company that fails to file annual confirmation or financial statements with the Registrar may be fined and struck off the Register; continuous failure can result in deregistration and disqualification of the director.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by an exempt Samoan International Company to non-resident shareholders. Ordinary resident companies paying dividends to non-residents are subject to a 15% dividend withholding tax unless a Double Taxation Agreement reduces the rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Where treaty relief is needed, the beneficial owner must obtain a Samoan Tax Residency Certificate from SIRCA, submit a completed WHT treaty relief declaration to the payer before the payment date, and attach a certificate of residence issued by the treaty partner's tax authority. SIRCA requires the declaration to include the recipient's legal name, TIN, treaty article, and confirmation of ownership of the income. For an exempt International Company, no withholding tax certificate is required for dividend distributions because domestic law imposes no Samoan tax; treaty relief is relevant only where the payment is sourced in Samoa or in a treaty country applying a domestic withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates are 15% for both interest and royalties paid to non-residents. Under Samoa's DTAs, interest is commonly reduced to 10% and royalties to 5%, with certain jurisdictions providing a 0% rate on royalties. International Companies are not subject to Samoan WHT on offshore royalty or interest payments, provided the payer is an exempt IC and the payment does not arise from Samoan-source commercial activity.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Related-party cross-border transactions exceeding WST 1,000,000 in a tax year trigger contemporaneous Transfer Pricing documentation, including a Local File and, if consolidated group revenue exceeds the applicable Group threshold, a Master File. For a tax-exempt International Company operating as an NVOCC, SIRCA may require the same documentation where such transactions involve commissions, container slot charters, or freight rebates with related parties and threaten to erode the Samoan tax base.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa's International Company regime does not impose full Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to Caribbean offshore centre rules, but the International Companies Act requires a registered office in Samoa, a licensed registered agent, maintenance of books and records, and commercially identifiable functions. For ocean freight forwarding ICs, SIRCA and foreign tax authorities will examine whether the IC has real decision-making, staff, bank accounts, and operational capacity. A pure mailbox NVOCC without substance is vulnerable to reclassification as a shell company, strike-off in Samoa, and CFC or anti-avoidance attack in the shareholder's residence jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Use of International Company Exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an International Company to invoice Samoan freight forwarding services performed by a local office or agent, concealing Samoan-source revenue, or filing a nil return while physically arranging cargo and collecting freight charges inside Samoa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act 2015 and Tax Administration Act 2012, SIRCA may issue a shortfall penalty of up to 100% of the tax avoided, impose late-payment charges up to 40%, and prosecute directors criminally. The Court may impose a fine of up to WST 1,000,000 and a term of imprisonment not exceeding 7 years, or both.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and registered agents who sign false declarations are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties. SIRCA can issue enforcement certificates, freeze bank accounts, impose travel bans, and remove directors from the International Company register.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Abusive Redomiciliation Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an NVOCC IC with no physical office, no employees, no Samoan bank account, and only a nominee agent, used as a conduit for trade-based money laundering or to shift profit from actual logistics operations located elsewhere.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Registrar of International Companies may cancel the certificate of incorporation, strike the company off the Register, and impose a fine not exceeding WST 50,000 plus daily default penalties. The company loses the right to enforce contracts in Samoan courts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable to creditors and to third-party cargo claimants where the company was used as an instrument of fraud. The Registrar may disqualify directors for up to 5 years and bar them from managing any Samoan company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register ultimate beneficial owners, refusing to conduct customer due diligence on NVOCC cargo clients, or moving freight payments through the Samoan IC account in layered transfers with no commercial rationale.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing legislation and the International Companies (Beneficial Ownership) rules, a company may be fined up to WST 500,000, have its bank accounts subject to freezing orders, and have its registered agent penalised and deregistered. Persistent breaches trigger regulatory review by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorise undocumented payments or false UBO declarations face imprisonment of up to 5 years, personal fines, and confiscation of assets. Travel bans may be imposed during criminal investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Economic Substance Misstatement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into related-party freight forwarding transactions with foreign affiliates where the Samoan IC earns a nominal commission while bearing no risk, owning no assets, and exercising no function, thereby attributing profit to an exempt entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SIRCA may disregard the arrangement, reattribute income to a taxable Samoan entity or to the entity exercising real functions, impose a substantial-compliance penalty of up to 50% of the underpaid tax, and charge interest. The exemption of the IC may be revoked retroactively if the transaction is found to be a sham.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who cause the IC to enter into artificial arrangements may be personally assessed for unpaid tax and penalties where they knowingly participated in the avoidance scheme. Civil restitution actions may be brought against them for the benefit of the revenue authority.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: DTA and Residency Shopping Abusive Treaty Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Obtaining a Samoan Tax Residency Certificate while the place of effective management of the NVOCC is in another country, then using the IC to claim treaty benefits on freight and logistics income in the source state.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The foreign tax authority may deny treaty benefits, impose the full domestic withholding tax rate, and request exchange of information from Samoa under the tax treaty or the Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance. Samoa may strike the IC off the Register for making false residency declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may become personally liable for the unpaid foreign withholding tax and fines under the source country's tax law. A finding of tax fraud may lead to extradition proceedings and imprisonment in the source jurisdiction if the conduct rises to deliberate domestic criminal tax evasion.
